result: Kind 1 of #23 matches the reference: a character cut short by end of input that began the read's input is an invalid sequence (WEOF, EILSEQ, bytes consumed); 2.39 and 2.41 agree on all 39+23 probe rows; kind 2 and kind 3 kept with reasons

gate.affected: 6741 passed / 0 failed (12 suites, 15 conformance programs, 0 SKIPPED)

rulings.item: +3 instr/call on 2-byte wide reads (fgetwc/getwc/fgetwc_unlocked_2byte 636->639, 646->649) from the fresh-fill note on a multibyte lead byte
rulings.recommendation: accept for the correctness fix; fix-forward: derive the flag in the cold end_of_input path from the buffer position and the pending length, so the hot path stays byte-for-byte

informational: Premise correction: kind 1 is not one rule on the reference. EILSEQ with the bytes consumed holds only when the cut-short character is the first input the read fetched (c3, e3 81, a x4096 then e3 81); after other buffered input the bytes come back with WEOF and feof, as D-12.28 recorded (its case had input before the character). 2.39 and stock trixie 2.41 are byte-identical on the 39-row table and the 23 boundary rows, so the reference version does not matter here

Kind 2 kept: matching needs the reference's wide-buffer convert-ahead chunking (boundary rows interleave byte and wide reads by internal chunk size) and an EOF with neither indicator set; the issue reproducer (97 252 99) and the col pass-through checks already match stock

Wide reads cost 7-11x the reference per call on this host (fgetwc_unlocked_2byte 639 vs 58.2, fgetwc_nul 366 vs 67.7); byte reads are at or below it (getc 24 vs 31). A wide-read fast path is a candidate story
SUPERSEDED: keke check1 (its clippy/static/so passed; the script stopped on a loader lookup), trixie and trixie2 (keyring setup; trixie3 ran the 2.41 probe)

impact.what: getwc on a stream whose input is only a cut-short multibyte character (c3; e3 81) returns WEOF with EILSEQ, error indicator set, bytes consumed, as on the reference (was WEOF, feof, bytes back); locale codec and ccs=UTF-8
conformance checks added to s12_wide_byte_reads.c (e3 81 alone, both encodings) and plants (5, all caught)
fgetwc_unlocked_2byte per call (wl_percall, Zen 1 host); getwc/fgetwc_2byte 646 -> 649; NUL, getc, fgetc, getc_unlocked rows unchanged (366/356/24/24/13); fix-forward in rulings

improvement: Yohane's differential probe should be a standing script in the tree (inputs x patterns, two references): this run rebuilt it from the issue text, and the D-12.28 vs #23 contradiction came from two different single cases, which a table would have shown at once
next_step: land; then fix-forward the +3 on 2-byte wide reads (flag derived in the cold path); Yohane's probe should then differ only in kind 2 and kind 3 rows
